metazoan influence on microbial carbonates is a major factor, and that the influence of seawater saturation state is a secondary factor.

metazoan influence has been a major factor in the decline of microbial carbonates since their Phanerozoically peak 500 Myyr ago, but that seawater chemistry and microbial evolution have been the major factors controlling their development throughout the Precambrian.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
microbial carbonates have been influenced by both the evolution of metazoan organisms and changes in seawater saturation state.
metazoans have influenced microbial carbonate abundance, but that the influence of seawater Ca2+ and CO32– concentrations has been more important.
metazoan and microbial competition and seawater saturation have been major influences on the development and preservation of microbial carbonate sediments during the Phanenoic Eon.
The main takeaway from our work is that
microbial carbonates are sensitive indicators of environmental change.
microbial carbonates have been important contributors to the Earth system for most of its history.
metazoan influence, together with seawater chemistry, have combined to determine microbial carbonate abundance throughout the Phanerozic.
